Package common.hardware.motorcontroller

Class NAR_Motor.MotorConfig

java.lang.Object
common.hardware.motorcontroller.NAR_Motor.MotorConfig
Enclosing class:
NAR_Motor
public static class NAR_Motor.MotorConfig extends Object
The hardware settings for a motor: what units it measures in, how much current it may draw, which way is forward, and whether it brakes when stopped.

  • Constructor Details

    • MotorConfig

      public MotorConfig(double distanceFactor, double timeFactor, int statorLimit, int supplyLimit, double voltageCompensation, boolean inverted, NAR_Motor.Neutral mode, NAR_Motor.StatusFrames statusFrames)
      Creates a motor config.
      Parameters:
      distanceFactor - Your position units per rotation of the encoder, which is usually the motor. For an arm in degrees on a 50:1 gearbox, 360.0 / 50; for an elevator in meters, the meters it rises per motor rotation.
      timeFactor - How many of your time units are in a minute: 60 for speeds per second, 1 for per minute.
      statorLimit - Most amps through the motor itself. This limits torque, so it stops mechanisms pushing too hard against hard stops and game pieces.
      supplyLimit - Most amps the motor controller draws from the battery. This protects the battery and breakers. Sparks don't have a true supply limit, so on a Spark this sets REV's secondary current limit instead, which briefly cuts output when the motor's current goes over it; see NAR_CANSpark.setSupplyLimit(int).
      voltageCompensation - Volts treated as full power, so output is the same as the battery drains. Usually 12.
      inverted - Whether positive output spins it clockwise instead of counterclockwise, looking at the motor's shaft.
      mode - Whether it brakes or coasts when told to stop.
      statusFrames - How often it reports its position and speed over CAN.
